name: Name
body: Battle Forge is a monthly series that presents a new WARMACHINE scenario in each installment. Battle Forge scenarios emphasize the narrative unfolding over the course of a game and may be asymmetrical, uneven, and even somewhat experimental because the goal of Battle Forge is to create a sandbox toolset that allows for creative scenario generation and new, story-worthy experiences with WARMACHINE! Players are encouraged to modify Battle Forge scenarios in any way that makes the scenario more appropriate for their army collections and their available terrain resources. Most important of all, have fun! And if you find a better way to do something with a scenario that results in a better experience for you, let us know at feedback@privateerpress.com, so we can try it, too!

name: Name
body: Following are the key terms that will be repeated in many Battle Forge scenarios:

name: Name
body: Many scenarios utilize objectives. An objective can either be a terrain piece, a marker, or a zone designated on a terrain piece or on the map.

name: Name
body: Objective Markers are impassable terrain features and should be represented on the table with markers that are at least 20 mm in diameter. Unless otherwise specified, all Objective Markers used in a scenario should be the same size.

name: Name
body: To have more models in an area than your opponent does.

name: Name
body: An area or objective is contested if both players have models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective at a time when scoring would take place. An area or objective is uncontested if only one player has models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective when scoring would take place.

name: Name
body: The zone or the area of a terrain feature is held when a player occupies the area with two or more models, uncontested.

name: Name
body: An objective terrain piece or marker is secured when a player has two or more models within 1" of the objective, uncontested.

name: Name
body: Battle Forge victories can be determined by either achieving the goals of the scenario or through Victory Points, scored in a variety of ways throughout playing a scenario. Turn limits on scenarios put pressure on players to succeed within a set amount of turns, and Victory Points provide the means to determine victory when neither player has completed the primary objective of a scenario.

name: Name
body:
In addition to its standard rules, each Battle Forge scenario has two random tables that add additional Victory Point-scoring opportunities for players that vary each time the scenario is played. Mission Modifiers add additional scoring opportunities based on the position of a player’s models on the table. Achievements add additional scoring opportunities based on a player’s actions taken on the battlefield.
Players should roll a d6 to randomly determine Mission Modifiers and Achievements before the beginning of a game, or players can choose them at will if all players agree. It is recommended that only one Mission Modifier and one Achievement should be in effect during any match (unless you really want to get crazy).

name: Name
body: If a player makes an attack that destroys one or more friendly models, that player’s opponent gains 1 Victory Point. If a player makes an attack and destroys their own Leader model, that player immediately loses the match.

name: Name
body: In addition to objectives, Battle Forge scenarios will routinely draw on the following terrain elements. Dimensions provided are approximations, and you should feel free to substitute any terrain pieces you have available as necessary. Use the resources you have available to get close enough to maintain the spirit and intention of the scenario.

name: Name
body: An obstacle with an approximate footprint of 3/4" x 4". Barriers provide cover.

name: Name
body: Obstructions with an approximate footprint of 5" x 5".

name: Name
body: Forest areas with an approximate footprint of 5" in diameter.

name: Name
body: An obstacle with an approximate footprint of 2" x 2". Small obstacles provide cover.

name: Name
body: An elevated platform at least 1" above the table, such as a hill or terrace. Plateaus can possess multiple areas at different heights that models can be placed on, but the areas must be level to prevent models from falling over. If a model cannot be placed on a level area without risk of falling off, it cannot occupy that area. Models cannot be placed on slopes, and we recommend that plateau terrain with sloped surfaces not be used. Plateau, Small— A plateau platform with a footprint approximately 6" in diameter and a level surface(s) at least 1" above the table that is large enough for five 30 mm models to be placed on. Plateau, Large— A plateau with a footprint approximately 6" to 12" in diameter and a level surface(s) at least 1" above the table that is large enough for five 40 mm models to be placed on.

name: Name
body: An area of shallow water approximately 6" in diameter.

name: Name
body: An area of rubble approximately 6" in diameter.

name: Name
body: A 3" x 5" trench template.

name: Name
body: Fill the bellies of your troops to fuel their fighting spirit!

name: Name
body: "Feast or Famine" is designed for 50-, 75-, and 100-point forces.

name: Name
body: "Feast or Famine" ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body: Players race to collect buried supply caches that can provide sustenance for their troops and fuel for their cohort as they work toward destroying their opponent’s bunker.

name: Name
body: Destroy the opponent’s bunker while gaining Victory Points for securing supply caches.

name: Name
body: This scenario uses 2 bunkers, 5 small plateaus, 5 small forests, 5 medium rubble fields, 1 large pond, 5 small walls, and 2 small obstacles on the table as shown on the map below. If you don’t have this exact assortment of terrain, use what you have to create a diverse environment with an emphasis on terrain that blocks line-of-sight across long distances. You’ll also need two each of 50 mm, 40 mm, 30 mm, and 20 mm scenario objectives.

name: Name
body:
"Feast or Famine" requires players to track food and fuel resources. Each player begins the game with three food tokens and three fuel tokens. At the beginning of a player’s turn, they must spend one food token if they have one or more units or solos in play and one fuel token if they have one or more Cohort models in play. If at any time a player has no food tokens, their units and solos become fatigued. If at any time a player has no fuel tokens, their Cohort models become fatigued.
Fatigued models suffer –2 SPD and DEF and –1 to their attack and damage rolls.
Supply cache objectives provide food and fuel tokens when secured.  Any combination of units, solos and Cohort models can secure a supply cache. A supply cache secured by only units and/or solos generates an additional +1 food token, and a supply cache secured by only Cohort models generates an additional +1 fuel token.Supply cache objectives are removed from the table after being secured.
50 mm supply caches must be secured by at least five models and provide 3 food and 3 fuel tokens when secured.

name: Name
body:
40 mm supply caches must be secured by at least four models and provide 2 food and 2 fuel tokens when secured.
30 mm supply caches must be secured by at least three models and provide 1 food and 1 fuel token when secured.
Once during each activation, a trooper model or solo can spend one food token to gain one of the following benefits:
The affected model gains +4 SPD during its Normal Movement.
The affected model can make one additional melee or ranged attack.
Once during each activation, a Cohort model can spend one fuel token to gain one of the following benefits:
The affected model gains +4 SPD during its Normal Movement.
The affected model can make one additional melee or ranged attack.
20 mm portable objectives are bombs which can be picked up as a special action by any Cohort model within 1" of it. Place the bomb objective next to the model carrying it. If a model carrying a bomb is destroyed, center the bomb on the destroyed model’s location before removing the destroyed model from the table. A model carrying a bomb can drop it at the start of its activation. When it does so, center the bomb on the dropping model’s current location. A model can only carry one bomb at a time. A model carrying a bomb cannot run.

name: Name
body:
A bomb placed on the top hatch of a bunker destroys the bunker.
Players score Victory Points each time they secure a supply cache objective:
- Score 1 Victory Point when securing a 20 mm objective
- Score 2 Victory Points when securing a 30 mm objective
- Score 3 Victory Points when securing a 40 mm objective
- Score 4 Victory Points when securing a 50 mm objective

name: Name
body: Roll once on both the Mission Modifiers and Achievement tables.

name: Name
body: Roll a d3 to determine the Mission Modifier for this match: 1. Eat What You Kill— Gain one food and one fuel token each time you destroy an enemy Cohort model. 2. Food Fight— Your opponent loses one food token each time you destroy the last model in a unit and one fuel token each time you destroy a Cohort model. 3. Harvest Season— Each time a supply cache is secured, place a new supply cache of the same size 12" away from the secured supply cache in a random direction.

name: Name
body: Roll a d3 to determine the Achievement for this match. 1. Fast Food— The first player to secure a 50 mm supply cache gains 1 Victory Point. 2. Hoarder— Gain 1 Victory Point once per game if you have five or more food tokens when your opponent has none, or five or more fuel tokens when your opponent has none. 3. Happy Thanksgiving— Gain 1 Victory Point each time you say out loud "Happy Thanksgiving" and give your opponent one food and one fuel token after destroying one of their Cohort models or the last model in one of their units.

name: Name
body: Victory conditions are checked in the following order: Decisive Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the only bunker in play wins. Point Advantage Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with 10 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match. Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the last Leader model in play wins the match. Victory Point Win: If neither player has a Leader in play or neither player has a bunker in play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match. At the end of six rounds, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match.
